study_identification_part.si4_title: Normative Modeling of Brain Morphometry in Clinical High Risk for Psychosis

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The paper clearly states its objective to quantify deviations from normative neuroanatomical variation in CHR-P and evaluate overlap with healthy variation and associations with positive symptoms, cognition, and conversion. It also explains the purpose of applying normative modeling in this context.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: OBJECTIVE To quantify deviations from the normative range ... and evaluate their overlap with healthy variation and their association with positive symptoms, cognition, and conversion to a psychotic disorder. ... Psychiatric neuroimaging has turned to normative modeling, which quantifies individual-level deviation ...

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: This study uses an existing normative model (CentileBrain) developed by the ENIGMA Lifespan Group. The original source is cited and the reference cohort is described as an independent multisite sample of 37,407 healthy individuals with age and sex summary. Transfer learning/recalibration was not performed. However, image quality/data completeness standards and exclusion reasons for the reference cohort are not detailed within this article.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: ... generated using a normative modeling framework ... (CentileBrain) ... developed by the ENIGMA Lifespan Group. The code and the models are publicly available ... the normative models ... were developed using data from an independent multisite sample of 37 407 healthy individuals (53.3% female; aged 3-90 years) ...

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: The normative framework explicitly optimized covariates and included site harmonization (ComBat-GAM) and global measures (intracranial volume, mean CT, mean SA) as covariates. This addresses age/sex via sex-specific models and multi-site effects via ComBat-GAM.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: Sex-specific normative models ... optimal covariate combination involved site harmonization (ComBat-GAM) and the inclusion of intracranial volume, mean CT, and mean SA ...
